title: Reality Defender brings real-time deepfake detection to the Microsoft Teams partner ecosystem
summary: Microsoft named Reality Defender a synthetic media detection partner for Teams. See how RealMeeting flags possible deepfakes during live meetings.
body_markdown:
With RealMeeting, the organizer can see detection results privately without leaving the meeting. If RealMeeting flags possible manipulation, the organizer can follow their organization’s policies to pause an approval, confirm a request through a trusted channel, or take additional steps to verify a candidate’s identity.


IT admins can make RealMeeting available across the organization or limit it to groups such as finance or recruiting. Once the app is available, organizers can turn it on in Teams for the meetings that need it. Participants join as usual, with no enrollment or voiceprint required.


RealMeeting analyzes short samples of meeting media for signs of AI manipulation as the conversation unfolds. The organizer sees the detection result and a confidence score in a private Teams side panel. If a scan flags possible manipulation, the organizer can respond in the moment according to their organization’s policies. After the meeting, authorized security teams can review the scan results in the Reality Defender dashboard and investigate any flags. Organizations with strict data requirements can turn on zero retention, which deletes meeting media after analysis.


Security teams can set a consistent standard for handling suspected impersonation across departments, and employees can keep doing sensitive work in the tools and workflows they already know.


[Explore RealMeeting on Microsoft Marketplace](https://marketplace.microsoft.com/en-us/product/WA200012072) **or**[contact us](https://www.realitydefender.com/get-in-touch) **to learn more about bringing real-time deepfake detection to your Microsoft Teams meetings.**
